approachQuestion.prompt:
Walk the Outer Fence

Return the outermost cells of a rectangular integer grid in clockwise order, starting at its top-left corner. Visit the top edge left to right, the right edge downward, the bottom edge right to left, and the left edge upward. Each position must appear exactly once, even when edges coincide in a one-row or one-column grid. Do not include interior cells.

Example 1: grid=[[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]] → [1,2,3,6,9,8,7,4].
Example 2: grid=[[1,2,3]] → [1,2,3].
Example 3: grid=[[4],[5],[6]] → [4,5,6].
Example 4: grid=[[8]] → [8].

Constraints:
1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000. Every row has length c.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9; equal values at different positions must each appear.
Do not modify grid. Return a fresh array of values.
constraints: 1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000. Every row has length c.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9; equal values at different positions must each appear.
Do not modify grid. Return a fresh array of values.

options.text: Append the top row. Append the rightmost column below it. If r>1, append the bottom row from column c−2 down to 0. If c>1, append the leftmost column from row r−2 down to 1.
options.feedback: The ranges exclude corners already emitted. The dimension guards prevent coincident edges from duplicating positions in a thin grid.

options.text: Walk top, right, bottom and left edges clockwise, including their corners. Maintain an r-by-c temporary Boolean matrix and append a position only on its first visit.
options.feedback: This produces the correct order and removes duplicate corner visits, but a full visited matrix is unnecessary when edge ranges are disjoint.

options.text: Append all four complete edges clockwise, including both corners of every edge, with no checks.
options.feedback: Corner positions are repeated, and thin grids repeat many more positions. [[8]] must return [8], not four copies.

options.text: Walk the edges clockwise and append a value only if that numeric value has not appeared earlier.
options.feedback: The rule is about positions, not distinct values. [[5,5]] requires [5,5], but value deduplication returns [5].

feedback.reason: Assign each corner to exactly one edge traversal.
details: Emit the top edge and then the right edge below it. Emit the remaining bottom edge only with multiple rows, then the remaining left edge only with multiple columns. Exclude corners already emitted.

Assign each corner to exactly one edge traversal. On a single row, top and bottom coincide; on a single column, left and right coincide. The conditional edge ranges avoid duplicate output without a visited set or any scan of interior cells.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Traverse Disjoint Edge Ranges”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let r,c be the dimensions. Indexed access is constant time; output append has amortized constant cost including resizing copies. Include output construction time. Exclude input and returned array/capacity; include loop variables and stack. No visited structure, recursion or hashing. Express the tight bound in r and c.
constraints: 1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000. Every row has length c.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9; equal values at different positions must each appear.
Do not modify grid. Return a fresh array of values.

options.text: O(r + c) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
O((r + c)²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Work follows the perimeter, with only fixed edge indices outside output.
details: The disjoint edge ranges emit exactly the perimeter positions. Their number is proportional to r+c, including one-dimensional grids and a single cell. Only fixed index state is stored beyond the returned array.
The option “O(r + c) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Work follows the perimeter rather than the area, without visited flags.
The option “O(r*c) time, O(r*c) auxiliary space.”: The fixed method neither scans nor marks interior cells.
The option “O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: The perimeter can grow with either dimension.
The option “O((r + c)²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Each perimeter position is emitted once, without rescanning previous output.
